Row 'Student (w/o Fine-tuning)' = the off-the-shelf GPT-J 6B student before any distillation (Sec. 4.2: 'we mainly utilize a publicly available LM GPT-J as our student LM'), prompted with fixed in-context demonstrations from the training set (App. A: 3-shot for GSM8K/MultiArith/SVAMP, 5-shot CSQA, 4-shot StrategyQA), greedy decoding; Table 1 marks this row 'CoT: No' (direct answers). Blevins, Gonen & Zettlemoyer, 'Prompting Language Models for Linguistic Structure' (ACL 2023). Table 6 (Full Results of GPT-Neo series experiments), row 'Model Size 6B, k=10', column 'NER (F1)' = 53.03 ± 1.0 (divided by 100). Structured prompting (Sec. 2): k = 10 demonstrations sampled from the training set, the model labels each word in turn with decoding constrained to the tag set (BIO constraints for NER), m = 5 runs with different demonstration sets, evaluated on a fixed random subset of 1,000 test examples per task (App. A.1). GPT-Neo series run from Hugging Face checkpoints by the authors ('We use the GPT-Neo models available through Huggingface'); Table 6 row labels give model size (125M/1.3B/2.7B GPT-Neo, 6B GPT-J, 20B GPT-NeoX). POS = UD English GUM UPOS accuracy; NER = CoNLL-2003 BIO tagging F1. Value before ±. 10-shot structured prompting with BIO-constrained per-token decoding on a fixed 1,000-example test subset (Sec. 3, App. A.1). GPT-J 6B per Sec. 3.3 ('6.7 billion parameters (Wang and Komatsuzaki, 2021)').

Printed cells carry a subscript standard deviation (e.g. '46.0' followed by subscript '1.5'); the mean is used.
